observations: For the architect, measured and not a failure: the new title decides three packages' next version, and one of them has no breaking change. .github/scripts/release-bump.sh:76 classifies a subject matching '^[a-z]+(\(.+\))?!:' as major, and the title matches. Each package's bump is scoped to the paths release.yaml's *_VERSION_ARGS name, and the merge touches all three: pi-envoy 16 files and pi-legion 13, both through packages/envoy-client/, whose shipped dispatch CLI really does lose a host, so a major there says something true; and the Go legion binary 1 file, packages/daemon/docker/worker.Dockerfile, one deleted COPY of a package that no longer exists. Nothing in the binary changes, so legion-v17.x would become v18.0.0 on a Dockerfile line. A scope on the title does not change it, since the regex matches with a scope and the path lists select the packages; dropping the '!' would make all three minor and would stop saying the CLI change is breaking. Which is right is a release-semantics call rather than a defect, and majors are evidently routine here (legion is already at v17). Named so the decision is made rather than discovered at the merge.
Rounds 1 and 2 left nothing open: the fabricated head SHA, the short A1 table and the missing refusal lock are all closed, and the lock was proven by mutation.
